battle.name: 米特里達梯戰爭
battle.theater: 龜甲半島、小亞細亞與希臘戰線
battle.brief: 前89年本都王米特里達梯六世攻入帕夫拉戈尼亞，驅走卡帕多西亞王阿里阿拉忒斯六世，羅馬先後派蘇拉、盧庫盧斯、龐培三名將領迎戰，三次戰爭延續二十六年，戰線由龜甲半島拉進希臘與亞美尼亞。卡面的斯巴達長矛已是希臘退場的形制，真正頂在本都方陣前端的是薩里沙長槍，而方陣的勝負依然由兩翼決定。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 米特里達梯戰爭（前89年至前63年）是羅馬共和國與本都王國之間長達二十六年的三次衝突，交戰重心在安納托利亞北部、奇里乞亞與卡帕多西亞，並兩度延伸到希臘本土與亞美尼亞高原。開戰的一方是本都王國：首都先在辛諾佩、後在阿米索斯，是黑海南岸一個希臘化程度很高的王國，國王米特里達梯六世把希臘城邦、馬其頓式的長槍方陣與龐大艦隊捏成一體。軍隊以薩里沙方陣步兵為骨幹，輔以「伙伴」重騎兵、蓋拉太傭兵、雙輪戰車、弓手與投石手，並在奇里乞亞海峽維持一支令地中海東岸畏懼的海盜艦隊。另一方是羅馬共和國：以執政官與行省總督為統帥，靠公民兵團與盟邦部隊作戰，先後得到比提尼亞、卡帕多西亞、帕加馬與羅得的支持，海上靠意大利沿海城邦的艦隊與希臘同盟艦隊。第三方是亞美尼亞王國：提格蘭二世先與米特里達梯結盟，後與之翻臉。塞琉古敘利亞、帕提亞與各個希臘城邦則在邊緣觀望或下注。本都內部也不是鐵板一塊，卡帕多西亞王族、黑海希臘城市與宮廷集團在這二十六年裡不斷倒戈，這是羅馬得以逐次捲入的縫隙。
countriesEn: The Mithridatic Wars (89–63 BC) were twenty-six years of conflict fought in three separate wars between the Roman Republic and the Kingdom of Pontus. The fighting centred on northern Anatolia, Cilicia and Cappadocia, and extended twice into mainland Greece and onto the Armenian plateau. One side was the Pontic kingdom: its capital was first Sinope and later Amisos, a highly Hellenised state on the southern shore of the Black Sea, and its king Mithridates VI had welded Greek poleis, a Macedonian-style pike phalanx and a very large fleet into a single instrument. Its army rested on phalanx infantry armed with the sarissa, supported by heavy Companion cavalry, Galatian mercenaries, scythed chariots, archers and slingers, and it kept a pirate fleet in the Cilician straits that the whole eastern Mediterranean feared. The other side was the Roman Republic, led by consuls and provincial governors, fighting with citizen legions and the contingents of its allies, with the backing of Bithynia, Cappadocia, Pergamon and Rhodes, and at sea with the fleets of the Italian coastal towns and of the Greek allies. The third party was the Armenian kingdom: Tigranes II was first Mithridates' ally and then his enemy. The Seleucid kingdom, Parthia and the Greek poleis watched from the edges or placed bets. Pontus was not solid ground either: the Cappadocian royal house, the Greek cities of the Black Sea and the court factions switched sides repeatedly during these twenty-six years, and that was the seam through which Rome was drawn in one war at a time.
people: 這場戰爭有兩位主角，一位是國王，一位是羅馬的將軍。米特里達梯六世·尤帕托爾約前135年生於辛諾佩，母親拉奧狄刻是塞琉古王朝的公主；他迎娶卡帕多西亞王阿里阿拉忒斯六世，先殺岳父、再殺妻兄，隨後把六名年幼王子全部處死，以免日後有人拿血統爭位，這些情節出自普魯塔克《蘇拉傳》。他從小被母親與宮廷包圍，成年後卻以自修聞名，據說通曉數門技藝，廣收希臘學者於宮中，又把本都的鑄幣與錢莊推成黑海最大的金融網絡，以重修辛諾佩、尼凱亞等城證明自己是黑海希臘世界的保護人。第三次戰爭失利後他退往克里米亞的博斯波魯斯王國，最終於前63年自殺。羅馬方面的核心人物是蘇拉：這位執政官在前88年接手東方戰事，用數年打崩本都的希臘戰線，卻在回師途中以自己的軍隊進攻羅馬，開啟共和國第一次內戰；他又是前83年以談判終結第二次戰爭的人，兩度證明這場戰爭可以不打。第一次戰爭裡有本都名將阿爾凱勞斯與羅馬偏將芬布里亞：前者在喀羅涅亞與奧爾科梅努斯兩敗於蘇拉，最終在前85年被芬布里亞陣殺；後者違抗蘇拉的休戰令擅自進攻，事後被蘇拉處死。第三次戰爭由盧庫盧斯與龐培接棒：盧庫盧斯以圍城與騎兵擾擾拖住本都，先後在蒂格拉諾塞塔、卡比拉與阿爾塔克薩塔擊敗亞美尼亞與本都的聯軍；龐培在清理地中海海盜後接手東線，用兩次側翼攻擊決定戰局。此外還有亞美尼亞王提格蘭二世，先結盟後反目；其弟阿爾塔夏斯三世的反叛直接扭轉東線；客戶王比提尼亞的尼科米德四世、卡帕多西亞的阿里巴拉內斯與帕加馬的歐墨內斯二世與阿塔洛斯三世，其忠誠與否也屢次改寫戰局。
peopleEn: This war had two principal figures, a king and a Roman general. Mithridates VI Eupator was born at Sinope about 135 BC; his mother Laodice was a princess of the Seleucid house. He married Ariarathes VI of Cappadocia, killed first his father-in-law and then his brother-in-law, and afterwards put six young princes to death so that no one could later claim the throne by blood; these episodes come down in Plutarch's Life of Sulla. Raised inside his mother's household and the court, he became famous as a self-educated man, said to have known several arts, and he gathered Greek scholars into his palace, built the coinage and banking of Pontus into the largest financial network on the Black Sea, and proved himself a protector of the Greek world there by rebuilding Sinope, Nicaea and other cities. After his defeat in the third war he withdrew to the Bosporan kingdom in Crimea and finally killed himself in 63 BC. The central figure on the Roman side was Sulla. The consul took over the eastern command in 88 BC, broke the Pontic position in Greece within a few years, and then turned his own army on Rome on the march home, opening the first civil war of the republic; he was also the man who ended the second war by negotiation in 83 BC, proving twice that this war did not have to be fought. The first war produced a famous Pontic general, Archelaus, and a hot-headed Roman legate, Fimbria: the first was beaten by Sulla at Chaeronea and at Orchomenus and was finally killed in action by Fimbria in 85 BC; the second disobeyed Sulla's order for a truce, attacked anyway, and was put to death by Sulla. The third war was taken over by Lucullus and Pompey. Lucullus wore the enemy down with sieges and cavalry raids, defeating the Armenian-Pontic coalition at Tigranocerta, Cabira and Artaxata; Pompey, after clearing the Mediterranean of pirates, inherited the eastern command and decided the campaign with two attacks on the flank. Around them stand Tigranes II of Armenia, first ally and then enemy, whose brother Artaxias III's defection turned the eastern front; and the client kings Nicomedes IV of Bithynia, Ariobarzanes of Cappadocia, and Eumenes II and Attalus III of Pergamon, whose loyalty changed the course of events more than once.
kits: 卡面是斯巴達長矛：兩米上下的白蠟木槍身，槍尾包銅套，重裝步兵方陣裡最便宜也最靠得住的武器。落到本場戰爭的年代，它已是退場的形制——希臘世界自前四世紀起改用馬其頓長槍，羅馬那邊則是重標槍與刺槍。但它在本役的位置恰恰是對照件：本都方陣前端真正握著的是薩里沙，即四米半到五米半的長槍，槍身修長，槍尾同樣帶金屬套，與卡面的形制同源；羅馬的刺槍則幾乎就是斯巴達長矛的直接後代，同為八尺白蠟木桿加鐵矛頭與尾刺，羅馬步兵正是靠它與短劍在近身混戰中收掉方陣的殘部。實際的裝備分兩邊說。本都一側：薩里沙方陣配小圓盾、青銅札甲與皮甲，「伙伴」重騎兵用長矛與鎧甲，蓋拉太傭兵用長身鐵劍與大盾，奇里乞亞海盜與本都艦隊用帶銅撞角的高舷樓船，攻城則有希臘工匠埃庇馬庫斯設計的巨型塔車赫勒波利斯，高約四十米、八層樓、數千人操作，可射箭投石，底層還能破門。羅馬一側：重標槍、短劍、弧面大盾、鎖子甲與皮甲、青銅與鐵盔，投石機與車載弩炮，以及每日挖壕築柵的野戰營壘；海上有三角艦與利布耳納快船，攻堅時用火船與噴水裝置對付港口防禦。糧秣上，本都靠隨軍大車隊與數十萬非戰鬥人員維持，羅馬靠海運從埃及與黑海運糧，蘇拉與盧庫盧斯都吃過補給線過長的苦頭。
kitsEn: The card shows a dory: a shaft of ash wood about two metres long with a bronze cap on the butt, the cheapest and most reliable weapon in the formation of the heavy infantry. By the time of this war it was a retired pattern: from the fourth century BC the Greek world had gone over to the Macedonian pike, and on the Roman side there were the heavy pilum and the thrusting hasta. Yet its place in this campaign is precisely as a reference piece. What the Pontic phalanx actually held at the front was the sarissa, a pike four and a half to five and a half metres long, slender in the shaft and likewise fitted with a metal cap at the butt, directly descended from the shape on the card; and the Roman hasta was very nearly the dory's own descendant, an eight-foot ash shaft with an iron head and a foot spike, the weapon with which the Roman infantry finished off the broken edge of the phalanx in close fighting alongside the gladius. The equipment in use can be set out on both sides. On the Pontic side: a sarissa phalanx with small round shields, bronze and leather armour, Companion heavy cavalry with long spears and armour, Galatian mercenaries with long iron swords and large shields, and Cilician pirates and Pontic warships with high hulls and bronze rams; for sieges there was the helepolis, the great tower designed by the Greek engineer Epimachus, about forty metres high and eight storeys, worked by thousands of men, able to shoot arrows and stones, with a battering head at its base. On the Roman side: the heavy pilum, the gladius, the curved oval scutum, chain and leather armour, bronze and iron helmets, stone-throwers and wagon-mounted ballistae, and the marching camp with its ditch and palisade dug every day; at sea the trireme and the fast liburna, and at the assault on ports, fire ships and water-spraying devices against the harbour defences. On supply: Pontus kept itself going with a huge baggage train and tens of thousands of non-combatants, while Rome depended on seaborne grain from Egypt and the Black Sea; both Sulla and Lucullus suffered badly from supply lines stretched too far.
tactics: 本都方陣的核心問題只有一個：長槍兵靠正面頂住敵人，兩翼一旦被繞過，整條長陣就會像紙牌屋一樣散掉。希臘人早知此事，安提柯留下過一句話，決定戰爭的是陣形的側面。米特里達梯在第三次戰爭採用「雙重陣」：步兵方陣在前，騎兵藏在後方，敵人露出哪一翼，隱藏的騎兵就從那一側殺出。羅馬人的解法同樣樸素——不與正面硬碰，而是讓步兵以大盾抵住長槍，等方陣鋒芒用盡、隊形被拉長，再以步兵中隊與精銳騎兵自側翼插進。前86年喀羅涅亞與奧爾科梅努斯兩役即是如此：本都騎兵多為雇傭兵，臨陣潰散，方陣側翼暴露，羅馬步兵與騎兵夾擊，長陣當場崩解。第二次戰爭則以攻守見長：前87至前86年羅馬軍圍攻雅典與比雷埃夫斯，用攻城塔、火船與噴水裝置強攻港口，雅典城破後遭到劫掠；同一期間本都軍在小亞細亞遭瘟疫，氣勢為之一挫。盧庫盧斯接手後改用消耗：刻意不求主力會戰，以騎兵襲擾糧道與海岸村落，逼米特里達梯在不利時機應戰，並一度追入亞美尼亞，切斷自己的補給線。龐培的破解更乾脆，兩次打側翼：前68年進攻亞美尼亞時以空心方陣抵禦箭雨，前67年澤拉一役用楔形縱隊正面撞擊方陣，前66年在里庫斯河谷以精銳部隊插入方陣側後，本都大軍隨即瓦解。海上則有另一套打法：史料記載本都曾把艦隊以陸路拖過山嶺，趕在追兵之前移入黑海，試圖用陸海轉移保住海上生存線，而羅馬的答案是不斷築城、逼近、封鎖口岸。
tacticsEn: The Pontic phalanx had only one central problem: the pike-holders won the front by weight, and once the flanks were turned the whole long line came apart like a house of cards. The Greeks knew this well; Antigonus left the remark that the flank decides the war. Mithridates answered it in the third war with the double formation: the phalanx in front, the cavalry hidden behind, and the hidden horse released against whichever side the enemy exposed. The Roman answer was equally plain: they did not meet the pike head on, but let the infantry hold the sarissas behind the big shields, waited for the phalanx's edge to dull and its order to stretch, and then drove in with cohorts and picked cavalry on the flank. That is how Chaeronea and Orchomenus were won in 86 BC: much of the Pontic horse was mercenary and simply ran, the flank of the phalanx lay open, and the Roman foot and horse struck together and the long line came down. The second war was won on the offensive and the defensive: in 87 and 86 BC the Roman army besieged Athens and the Piraeus, using siege towers, fire ships and water-spraying devices against the harbour, and sacked Athens after it fell; in the same period disease broke out among the Pontic army in Asia Minor and took the edge off its offensive. Lucullus changed the method and went for exhaustion: he deliberately refused a general engagement, raided supply lines and coastal villages with cavalry, forced Mithridates to fight on ground of his choosing, and at one point pursued into Armenia and cut his own supply behind him. Pompey's solution was blunter still and worked twice through the flank: advancing on Armenia in 68 BC he used a hollow square against the arrows, at Zela in 67 BC he drove a wedge straight into the phalanx, and in the valley of the Lycus in 66 BC he sent picked troops round the rear of the phalanx, and the Pontic army dissolved. At sea there was a different set of answers: the sources record that Pontus once dragged its fleet overland across the mountains to move it into the Black Sea ahead of its pursuers, trying to save its line of existence at sea by shifting between land and water, and Rome's answer was to keep building fortified towns, closing in, and sealing the harbours.
data: 留下數字的地方集中在雙方的戰報殘片與後世史家的估算上，讀的時候要留神敵方帳目。時間最清楚：三次戰爭自前89年打到前63年，合計二十六年；第一次約前88至前84年，第二次前83至前81年，第三次前74至前63年，兩次中間隔著六到七年的和平，但雙方都沒有真正罷手。兵力方面，蘇拉出發時被授予兩個軍團的編制，另有帕加馬、羅得、卡帕多西亞與比提尼亞提供的部隊，他在喀羅涅亞作戰時實際能指揮的兵力在萬餘量級。本都方陣步兵的核心，古代史家一般記作一萬五千上下，輔以「伙伴」騎兵數千、雙輪戰車數千輛（其中帶鐮刀者數千輛、披甲者百餘輛），弓手與投石手另計。普魯塔克與阿庇安記載第三次戰爭初期本都軍步兵約十萬至十二萬、騎兵約一萬五千至兩萬，並說連同非戰鬥人員的軍營合計達三十萬量級；這些都是敵方視角的數字，多半把工匠、隨軍商販與奴隸一併算入，盧庫盧斯一側則常被記作一萬五千上下的步兵與數千騎兵。距離與時間方面，這場戰爭把羅馬的戰場推到地中海東岸最遠處：自羅馬至亞美尼亞的蒂格拉諾塞塔單程約三千五百公里，軍隊按日行二十五至三十公里計，最少也要走上四個月；本都的辛諾佩到雅典海路約一千一百公里。圍攻雅典與比雷埃夫斯耗時約一年，赫勒波利斯造了八個月。損失方面，蘇拉的回憶錄與普魯塔克都記載本都軍在小亞細亞遭瘟疫，後世引用的死亡數字高達十餘萬乃至數十萬，但顯然含非戰鬥人員，只能當量級參考。最後是行政數字：前63年龐培把比提尼亞與本都合為一個行省，這是羅馬在黑海南岸取得的永久版圖。
dataEn: The numbers that survive come from fragments of battle reports on both sides and from later estimates by historians, and they have to be read with care because so many of them are enemy figures. The chronology is the clearest thing of all: the three wars run from 89 to 63 BC, twenty-six years in total; the first from about 88 to 84 BC, the second from 83 to 81 BC, the third from 74 to 63 BC, with six or seven years of peace between them during which neither side truly stood down. On strength: Sulla was given the establishment of two legions when he set out, together with contingents supplied by Pergamon, Rhodes, Cappadocia and Bithynia, and the force he actually commanded at Chaeronea was on the order of ten thousand men. The core of the Pontic phalanx is generally given by the ancient historians as about fifteen thousand, with several thousand Companion cavalry, several thousand chariots of which some thousands carried scythes and a few score hundred were armoured, and archers and slingers counted separately. Plutarch and Appian put the Pontic army at the opening of the third war at roughly one hundred to one hundred and twenty thousand foot and fifteen to twenty thousand horse, and describe the camp including non-combatants as reaching three hundred thousand; these are enemy-side figures that fold in craftsmen, camp followers and slaves, while Lucullus's own side is usually recorded at about fifteen thousand foot and some thousands of horse. On distance and time: this war carried the Roman battlefield to the far end of the eastern Mediterranean. The road from Rome to Tigranocerta in Armenia is about three thousand five hundred kilometres, and at the twenty-five to thirty kilometres a day of a marching army it was at least four months on the road; the sea passage from Sinope to Athens is about eleven hundred kilometres. The siege of Athens and the Piraeus took roughly a year, and the helepolis took eight months to build. On losses: Sulla's memoirs and Plutarch both record disease breaking out among the Pontic army in Asia Minor, and the death figure quoted by later writers runs to a hundred thousand and beyond, but it plainly includes non-combatants and can only be used as an order of magnitude. Last, an administrative number: in 63 BC Pompey joined Bithynia and Pontus into a single province, and that is the permanent Roman acquisition on the southern shore of the Black Sea.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層，每一層都跟羅馬有關。第一層是王位的殺局：米特里達梯六世迎娶卡帕多西亞王阿里阿拉忒斯六世後，先殺岳父、再殺妻兄，隨後把六名年幼王子全部處死，以免有人將來拿血統爭位；他的母親拉奧狄刻不甘心讓兒子受制，一度試圖毒殺他未果，後來反被兒子用釋放之人的手毒死。米特里達梯早年兵不多，這讓他更緊緊抓著婚姻與繼承這條繩子。第二層是羅馬的東方政策：前二世紀末，羅馬已把比提尼亞與卡帕多西亞收為客戶國，把希臘城邦的城防與海上航線視為自己的利益；本都王國在黑海東岸擴張，扶植自己的駐軍與艦隊，與羅馬的客戶國直接接壤，衝突遲早要爆。蘇拉之所以在前88年被派出去，官方理由是比提尼亞王尼科米德四世遭侵略、卡帕多西亞王位被推翻。第三層是第三次戰爭的引信：前67年龐培清剿奇里乞亞海盜，直接摧毀本都的經濟命脈與船隊，而本都在黑海的小國與商路本來就靠航運與掠奪撐起；等盧庫盧斯接手，米特里達梯已無退路，只能再攻亞美尼亞、搶黑海，把第三次戰爭打成破釜沉舟的東征。龐培在書信中把對方的計畫說成要把整個亞洲米特拉達梯化，薩魯斯特寫給西塞羅的信更把這種恐懼寫成羅馬政治語言裡最常見的警號。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause, and every one of them ran through Rome. The first was a killing at the level of the succession: after Mithridates VI married Ariarathes VI of Cappadocia he killed his father-in-law and then his brother-in-law, and afterwards put six young princes to death so that no one could later claim the throne by blood. His mother Laodice would not bear being ruled by her son and tried to poison him without success, and was then herself poisoned by a freedman in his pay. Mithridates had few soldiers of his own in those early years, and that was exactly why he held so tightly to the thread of marriage and inheritance. The second layer was Roman policy in the East: by the close of the second century BC Rome had taken Bithynia and Cappadocia as client kingdoms, treated the defences of the Greek cities and the sea lanes as its own interest, and stood directly alongside the expanding Pontic kingdom, whose garrisons and warships in the eastern Black Sea touched Roman client states. A collision was only a matter of time. Sulla was sent east in 88 BC officially because Nicomedes IV of Bithynia had been invaded and the king of Cappadocia had been driven from his throne. The third layer is the trigger of the third war: in 67 BC Pompey's clearance of the Cilician pirates destroyed the economic base and the fleet of Pontus outright, and the little kingdoms and the trade of the Black Sea had always rested on shipping and plunder; and by the time Lucullus took over, Mithridates had no way back, so he struck at Armenia again and fought for the Black Sea, turning the third war into a war of no return. Pompey described the opposing plan in his letters as an attempt to Mithridatise the whole of Asia, and Sallust's letters to Cicero turned that fear into the most common warning in the political language of Rome.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果一半在戰場之外，而且往後延續了幾十年。制度上最要緊的一條：蘇拉前88年帶著東方的軍隊與錢回師羅馬，沿途強行解決退役與軍餉問題，最終兵臨城下，共和國第一次內戰由此開打；此後羅馬的將軍第一次發現，遠征帶回的戰利品與軍隊本身就是權力的來源。軍隊的職業化也從此定型，士兵在軍中服役的年限被限制，軍團不再只是臨時召集的公民，這套做法在往後數十年裡一直是羅馬東征的底子。版圖上，希臘化時代最後幾個大國之一就此消失：本都在第三次戰爭後被拆成客戶地與行省（比提尼亞與本都行省，前63年），克里米亞的博斯波魯斯王國由米特里達梯的兒子法爾納塞斯二世接管，成為羅馬在黑海的另一枚棋子；亞美尼亞淪為附庸；黑海希臘城市得到保留，辛諾佩與卡帕多西亞的城防與鑄幣業被羅馬接管，這些城在往後幾個世紀成為希臘文化在北方的重要支點。經濟與社會上，被販賣的東方人口大量流入羅馬與希臘市場；龐培東征歸來的炫富在前61年成為共和國晚期的政治事件；財富集中與軍隊私人化，終於把羅馬推向內戰與帝制。心態上，米特里達梯成了羅馬政治裡一個固定的反面典型：貪婪、殘酷、以為自己能靠軍隊與金錢對抗元老院；這種恐懼在共和國末期被不斷引用，也正因如此，當西塞羅在演說裡提到「米特拉達梯」，聽眾立刻知道他指的是什麼。
impactEn: Half the consequences of this war lay off the battlefield, and they ran on for decades afterwards. The most important institutional consequence: in 88 BC Sulla marched back to Rome with his eastern army and his eastern money, forced the questions of discharge and arrears as he came, and finally brought his troops to the walls of the city, and the first civil war of the republic began there. From that moment Roman generals discovered for the first time that the plunder and the army brought back from a campaign were themselves a source of power. The professionalisation of the army was fixed at the same time: the length of a soldier's service was bounded, the legion was no longer only a levy of citizens called out for the occasion, and that arrangement was the foundation of Roman campaigning for the decades to come. On the map, one of the last great states of the Hellenistic age disappeared: after the third war Pontus was broken up into client territories and a province, Bithynia and Pontus in 63 BC, while the Bosporan kingdom in Crimea passed to Mithridates' son Pharnaces II and became another Roman client on the Black Sea; Armenia was reduced to subjection; the Greek cities of the Black Sea survived, and the defences and coinage of Sinope and Cappadocia were taken over by Rome, those cities remaining for the next several centuries the northern anchor of the Greek world. Economically and socially, large numbers of the people of the East were sold into the markets of Rome and Greece; the parade of Pompey's eastern plunder in 61 BC became an event of late republican politics; and the concentration of wealth together with the privatisation of the armies pushed Rome towards civil war and empire. In the mind, Mithridates became a fixed negative type in Roman politics, greedy, cruel, and certain that his armies and his money could stand against the senate; the fear of him was quoted again and again in the last years of the republic, and it was for that reason that when Cicero named Mithridates in a speech the audience knew at once what was meant.
result: 結果是本都王國的徹底崩解，以及羅馬在東方的得手。前66年龐培在里庫斯河谷擊潰本都大軍，米特里達梯帶著妻兒與部將退入博斯波魯斯王國，在那裡又撐了三年：他的兩個兒子相繼死去，舊部策劃逃亡，宮廷也發生分裂。前63年他終於在絕境中服毒自盡，據說用自己的牙齒咬破毒藥；頭顱被送到羅馬送給凱撒，遺體則由龐培的兒子護送回羅馬，安葬在龐培家族的墓園裡。前63年龐培把比提尼亞與本都合為一個行省，本都舊地就此進入羅馬的稅冊；提格蘭二世不久也走到生命盡頭，亞美尼亞淪為羅馬附庸；博斯波魯斯王國由法爾納塞斯二世統治，父子相傳，成為羅馬在北方最長久的客戶。戰爭的技術層面也有收穫：羅馬人第一次認真地把破方陣當成科目來做，側翼攻擊與投射武器的運用被寫進軍制；希臘的攻城機械傳統，像赫勒波利斯那樣的巨型塔車，也落進羅馬工程兵的技藝庫。從地緣上看，羅馬拿到的不是一個省，而是一整條從愛琴海到黑海東岸的海陸帝國骨架；這副骨架在往後一百年裡，再沒被任何一個希臘化王國動搖過。
resultEn: The outcome was the complete collapse of the Pontic kingdom and the gain of the East for Rome. In 66 BC Pompey broke the Pontic army in the valley of the Lycus, and Mithridates withdrew with his wives, his children and his generals into the Bosporan kingdom, where he held on for three more years: two of his sons died, his old officers plotted an escape, and his own household split. In 63 BC he finally took poison in his extremity, biting the poison open with his own teeth, as the story has it; his head was carried to Rome and given to Caesar, while his body was escorted home by Pompey's son and buried in the family tomb of the Pompeii. In 63 BC Pompey joined Bithynia and Pontus into one province, and the old lands of Pontus entered the Roman tax registers; Tigranes II did not long survive either, and Armenia became a Roman client; the Bosporan kingdom was ruled by Pharnaces II, father and son in succession, and became Rome's longest-lived client in the north. The war also had technical dividends: for the first time the Romans took breaking the phalanx seriously as a subject, and the flanking attack and the use of missile weapons were written into their military system; and the Greek tradition of siege machinery, giant tower wagons like the helepolis, passed into the repertoire of the Roman engineers. Geopolitically, what Rome gained was not a province but the skeleton of a maritime and land empire reaching from the Aegean to the eastern Black Sea, and for a century afterwards that skeleton was never again shaken by any Hellenistic kingdom.
